title: Delete N Nodes After M Nodes of a Linked List
statement:
`head` is the first node of a non-empty singly linked list, and `m` and `n` are positive integers. Walk the list from the head and thin it out with a repeating pattern: hold on to the next `m` nodes, then cut out the `n` nodes that follow them, then hold on to `m` more, cut `n` more, and so on until the list runs out. If fewer nodes remain than a step asks for, that step simply takes all of them.

Return the head of the list that is left (the surviving nodes stay in their original order).
constraints: The list has between 1 and 10^4 nodes
signature: ListNode deleteNodes(ListNode head, int m, int n)
notes:
## Intuition

The simplest idea is to copy the values out, keep those whose index modulo `m + n` is below `m`, and build a new list. But the pattern only ever looks ahead by `m + n` nodes, so it can be done in place: walk to the last node of each kept block, then jump its `next` pointer over the following `n` nodes in one relink.

## Approach

1. Put `last` on the head; it always points at the first node of a block to keep.
2. Advance `last` up to `m - 1` times so it rests on the final kept node of this block (stopping early if the list ends).
3. Start `next` just after `last` and step it forward up to `n` times, passing over the nodes to delete.
4. Link `last.next = next`, which drops every skipped node at once.
5. Continue from `next`, the first node of the following kept block, until it is `null`. Return `head`, which is never deleted.

## Example 1, step by step

The list is `1 -> 2 -> ... -> 13`, `m = 2`, `n = 3`.

- `last` starts on `1`, moves to `2`. `next` passes `3, 4, 5` and stops on `6`; link `2 -> 6`.
- `last` is `6`, moves to `7`. `next` passes `8, 9, 10` and stops on `11`; link `7 -> 11`.
- `last` is `11`, moves to `12`. `next` passes `13` and becomes `null`; link `12 -> null`.

The result is `[1, 2, 6, 7, 11, 12]`.

## Complexity

- Time: O(L) for a list of L nodes: every node is stepped over once, either by `last` or by `next`.
- Space: O(1): only two pointers and two counters.

## Pitfalls

- The kept loop starts counting at 1 because `last` already stands on the first kept node; starting at 0 keeps `m + 1` nodes.
- Check `last.next !== null` and `next !== null` before stepping, since the final block may be shorter than `m` or `n`.
- Relink once after skipping, rather than unlinking nodes one at a time, to keep the code simple and correct.

## Variables

| Name | Meaning |
|---|---|
| `last` | the node being kept; after the first loop, the last kept node of the block |
| `kept` | how many nodes of the current block have been kept |
| `next` | the first node after the deleted run (or `null`) |
| `removed` | how many nodes of the current run have been skipped |
